t.6.60.1: Then the hosts of rākṣasas who had survived the slaughter there quickly reported to Rāvaṇa that those bulls among rākṣasas, Devāntaka, Triśiras, Atikāya and the others, had been slain.
t.6.60.2: Then, suddenly hearing that they had been slain, the king, his eyes flooded with tears, fell into a swoon; and reflecting on the dreadful destruction of his sons and the slaying of his brothers, the king brooded deeply.
t.6.60.3: Then, seeing the king dejected and sinking deep in an ocean of grief, Indrajit, the bull among rākṣasas and son of the rākṣasa king, spoke these words.
t.6.60.4: Father, you should not give way to despair while Indrajit lives, O lord of the rākṣasas, for no one struck by the arrows of Indra's foe can keep hold of his life in battle.
t.6.60.5: Behold today Rāma, together with Lakṣmaṇa, his body pierced and torn apart by my arrows, lying lifeless on the surface of the earth, all his limbs covered with sharp shafts.
t.6.60.7: Today Indra, Vaivasvata, Viṣṇu, Mitra, the Sādhyas, the Aśvins, Vaiśvānara, Candra and Sūrya shall behold my immeasurable and fierce valour, like that of Viṣṇu in the sacrificial enclosure of Bali.
t.6.60.6: Hear this firmly resolved vow of Śakra's enemy, backed by both human valor and divine favor: this very day I shall torment Rāma, together with Lakṣmaṇa, with my unfailing arrows.
t.6.60.8: Having spoken thus, the foe of the lord of the thirty gods, of undaunted spirit, took leave of the king and mounted his chariot, swift as the wind, well harnessed with the finest donkeys.
t.6.60.9: Mounting a chariot like the chariot of Hari, the greatly radiant subduer of foes went at once to the place where the battle was raging.
t.6.60.10: As that great-souled one set out, many mighty warriors followed him, rejoicing, with excellent bows in their hands.
t.6.60.11: Some were mounted on the shoulders of elephants, some on excellent horses, bearing darts, hammers, swords, battle-axes and maces.
t.6.60.12: Amid the fearsome blasts of conches and the mighty roar of kettledrums, that foe of the lord of the thirty gods went forth, being praised by the night-roamers.
t.6.60.13: That destroyer of foes shone with his parasol, white as a conch or the moon, just as the sky shines with the full moon.
t.6.60.14: Then the hero, foremost among all bowmen, was fanned with excellent, beautiful golden whisks adorned with gold.
t.6.60.15: Then Laṅkā shone with Indrajit, whose splendor was like the sun's and whose valor was unrivaled, as the sky shines with the radiant sun.
t.6.60.16: But the glorious Rāvaṇa, lord of the Rākṣasas, seeing his son setting forth surrounded by a mighty army, spoke to him.
t.6.60.18: Thus addressed by the lord of the Rākṣasas, the hero received his great blessings and, swiftly going by a chariot yoked with horses, reached Nikumbhilā.
t.6.60.17: You are without a rival, my son; even Vāsava was conquered by you in battle. How much more, then, will you not slay Rāghava, a mere man who can easily be overcome?
t.6.60.19: Having reached the battlefield, that greatly splendid subduer of foes stationed the rākṣasas all around his chariot.
t.6.60.21: There the mighty lord of the rākṣasas made offerings into the fire with oblations, nets, and sacred rites, accompanied by garlands and fragrances.
t.6.60.20: Then the foremost of the rākṣasas, whose splendor was like that of fire, made offerings into the fire, the eater of oblations, with the proper mantras and according to the prescribed rites.
t.6.60.22: Weapons served as the reed-leaves, and there were fuel-sticks and vibhītaka wood, red garments, and likewise a ladle made of black iron.
t.6.60.23: There he spread arrow-feathers and lances around the fire, and seized by the throat a goat, entirely black and still alive.
t.6.60.24: Of the fire, kindled but once, smokeless and great-flamed, there arose those signs which foretold victory.
t.6.60.25: Rising up of his own accord, the Fire, its flames turning in auspicious circles to the right and gleaming like molten gold, accepted that oblation.
t.6.60.26: He, the foremost of those skilled in weapons, summoned the Brāhma weapon, and there he consecrated everything with mantras, his bow and his own chariot as well.
t.6.60.27: As that missile was being invoked and oblations were being poured into the fire, the vault of the sky, with its sun, planets, moon and stars, trembled in fear.
t.6.60.29: Leaving his own army behind and swiftly closing in on the hosts of monkeys in that great battle, he, remaining unseen, rained down a fierce net of arrows, as a dark rain-cloud pours down water.
t.6.60.28: He, blazing with a splendour like that of fire and equal in might to great Indra, made offerings into the fire, and then, of inconceivable form, he made himself vanish in the sky together with his bow, arrows, sword, chariot, horses and charioteer.
t.6.60.30: Those monkeys, huge as mountains, their bodies torn apart by the arrows of Śakrajit and struck down by his magic, fell on the battlefield crying out discordantly, like lordly mountains smitten by Indra's thunderbolt.
t.6.60.31: In the battle, amid the monkey armies, they saw only the sharp-pointed arrows; but the foe of the lord of the gods, hidden by illusion, that rākṣasa they did not see there.
t.6.60.32: Then that great-souled lord of the rākṣasas covered all the directions with hosts of sharp-tipped arrows radiant as the sun, and he cast the chiefs of the vānaras into despair.
t.6.60.33: Whirling spears, swords and battle-axes that resembled blazing fire, ablaze with flames and showering sparks, he rained them fiercely upon the army of the lord of the monkeys.
t.6.60.34: Then the leaders of the vānara troops, struck by the sharp arrows of Śakrajit that blazed like fire, looked like kiṃśuka trees in full bloom.
t.6.60.35: Pierced through by the missiles of the lord of the Rākṣasas, the bulls among the monkeys fell, crawling toward one another and crying out in discordant voices.
t.6.60.36: Some, gazing up at the sky, were struck in the eyes by arrows; they stumbled into one another and fell upon the surface of the earth.
t.6.60.37: Hanumān and Sugrīva, Aṅgada and Gandhamādana, Jāmbavān and Suṣeṇa, and Vegadarśin as well.
t.6.60.38: Mainda and Dvivida, Nīla, Gavākṣa, Gaja and Gomukha, Kesarin, Harilomān, and the monkey Vidyuddaṃṣṭra.
t.6.60.39: Sūryānana and Jyotirmukha, and likewise the monkey Dadhimukha, Pāvakākṣa and Nala, and also the vānara Kumuda.
t.6.60.40: With lances, pikes and sharp arrows charged with mantras, Indrajit, the foremost of rākṣasas, pierced all those tigers among monkeys.
t.6.60.41: Having shattered the foremost leaders of the monkey troops with maces and with arrows whose shafts were feathered with gold, he rained upon Rāma, together with Lakṣmaṇa, dense nets of arrow-showers that blazed like the rays of the sun.
t.6.60.42: Being showered with torrents of arrows, yet regarding them as mere downpours of rain, Rāma of supremely wondrous splendour, looking on, then spoke thus to Lakṣmaṇa.
t.6.60.44: Granted a boon by Svayambhū, the mighty Indrajit has taken his stand in the sky, his terrible body hidden from sight. Bodiless in battle, with his weapon raised, how indeed can he be slain today?
t.6.60.43: But this lord of the rākṣasas, O Lakṣmaṇa, the foe of the lord of the gods, relying on the Brahmāstra, has struck down the fierce monkey army and now torments us relentlessly with his arrows.
t.6.60.45: I think it is the blessed, inconceivable Self-existent One to whom this weapon belongs and who is its source. So today, O wise one, with an untroubled mind, endure here along with me the falling of these arrows.
t.6.60.46: For this lord of the Rākṣasas is covering all the directions with nets of showering arrows, and this entire army of the king of the Vānaras, its foremost heroes fallen, no longer shines.
t.6.60.47: Seeing the two of us fallen and senseless, withdrawn from the fight, our wrath and our joy destroyed, he will surely enter the dwelling of the enemy of the immortals, carrying off with him the glory of the forefront of battle.
t.6.60.48: Then the two of them were cut down there by the nets of Indrajit's missiles; and he, the lord of rākṣasas, having struck the two down there, roared with joy in the battle.
t.6.60.49: Then, having thrown that army of the king of the vānaras, and Rāma together with Lakṣmaṇa, into dejection on the field of battle, he swiftly entered the city guarded by the arms of Daśagrīva.
